```{r, include = FALSE}
has_deps <- requireNamespace("bio3d", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("NGLVieweR", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.align = "center",
  eval = has_deps
)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = !has_deps, results = "asis"}
cat("This vignette needs the bio3d and NGLVieweR packages. ",
    "Install them with install.packages(c(\"bio3d\", \"NGLVieweR\")).", sep = "")
```

`plot_hdx_structure()` colors a protein structure by HDX data, directly in R.
It shows an interactive 3D view that can be rotated, saved, or put into a report.
To color structures in PyMOL instead, use the `pymol_script_*()` functions (see `vignette("HDXBoxeR")`).

The function needs the bio3d and NGLVieweR packages.
They are optional and are not installed with HDXBoxeR.

## What is colored

The input is per-residue data from `residue_level_average()` or `residue_deconvolution()`.
For one time point, each residue is colored by the difference `state2 - state1`.
The colors are the same red/blue scale as the heat maps.
Residues without data are grey.

## Example

```{r}
library(HDXBoxeR)
file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a <- output_tp(file_nm, percent = TRUE)
res <- residue_level_average(a, protein_length = 225)
```

The structure below is **not** the protein of the example data.
It is lysozyme (`1HEL`), a small structure that comes with bio3d, used only to show how the function works.
Use the PDB of your own protein.

```{r fig_structure_basic}
pdb_demo <- system.file("examples", "1hel.pdb", package = "bio3d")
plot_hdx_structure(res, pdb = pdb_demo, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound",
                   times = "1800.00s", chain = "A")
```

The legend is drawn separately with `plot_hdx_structure_legend()`, using the same `ranges`:

```{r fig_structure_legend, fig.width = 3, fig.height = 4}
res_1800 <- res[res$Deut.Time == "1800.00s", ]
delta <- rowMeans(res_1800[, grep("^bound", colnames(res_1800))], na.rm = TRUE) -
  rowMeans(res_1800[, grep("^Unbound", colnames(res_1800))], na.rm = TRUE)
step <- max(abs(delta), na.rm = TRUE) / 3
plot_hdx_structure_legend(c(-Inf, -3*step, -2*step, -step, 0, step, 2*step, 3*step, Inf),
                          unit_label = "% Deut")
```

## Residue numbering

If the HDX numbering and the PDB numbering differ (for example because of a tag), use `resno_offset`.
It is added to every residue number before matching the PDB.
The same argument exists in the `pymol_script_*()` functions.

## Good to know

-   Residues are colored by the size of the difference, not by significance. For significant residues only, use `pymol_script_significant_residue()`.
-   One time point and one pair of states per call.
